nodes.title: SG-10.2.2 Scene applies the store's focused object as hover highlight and label
nodes.body:
Context: gameStore already holds focusedObjectId and setFocusedObject (SG-10.2.1), and SceneObject.focus()/blur() already draw the same highlight and label as hover. BootScene does not read focusedObjectId yet. Desired behavior: the scene reads the store focus value on each store change, focuses the matching SceneObject, and clears focus when the value is null. Expected result: a unit test with Phaser mocked proves it. Why: so keyboard focus held in the store appears on the canvas.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given focusedObjectId is 'bookshelf' when the store changes then the SceneObject with spec.id 'bookshelf' has focus() called
- Given focusedObjectId becomes null then every focused SceneObject has blur() called
- A unit test with Phaser mocked covers both cases


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene store subscription applies focusedObjectId to SceneObjects
- In scope: Unit test with Phaser mocked
- Out of scope: Writing focusedObjectId from the keyboard handler
- Out of scope: Changing gameStore
- Out of scope: Changing SceneObject or the engine
- Preserve: Existing hover behavior
- Preserve: Existing keyboard handling and focusChange event
- Preserve: BootScene shutdown cleanup


## Technical constraints
- Reuse SceneObject.focus() and blur(); do not add new highlight code
- Phaser 3.90; Phaser is mocked in unit tests


## Definition of done
- Both requirements verified by passing unit tests


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene focuses the object matching the store focusedObjectId
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.onStateChange only syncs objects with GameState. Desired behavior: on each store change it reads focusedObjectId and calls focus() on the SceneObject whose spec.id equals it. Expected result: that object shows the hover highlight and label. Why: store-driven focus must reach the canvas.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given focusedObjectId 'bookshelf' and a SceneObject with spec.id 'bookshelf' when the store notifies then that object's focus() is called
- Given focusedObjectId names a different object then the 'bookshelf' object's focus() is not called


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene focus application
- Out of scope: Keyboard handler writes
- Preserve: sceneObjects sync(state) calls


## Technical constraints
- Match by SceneObject.spec.id


## Dependencies
- INT-1


## Definition of done
- BootScene focuses the matching object on store change

- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene clears focus when the store focusedObjectId is null
nodes.body:
Context: SceneObject.blur() removes highlight and label. Desired behavior: when focusedObjectId is null (or matches no object), every currently focused SceneObject is blurred, and this runs even before GameState is initialised. Expected result: no object stays highlighted. Why: clearing focus in the store must clear the canvas.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a focused SceneObject and focusedObjectId set to null when the store notifies then its blur() is called
- Given focusedObjectId is null and no object is focused then neither focus() nor blur() is called


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene clearing logic and wiring into onStateChange
- Out of scope: SceneObject changes
- Preserve: Early return when GameState is null must not skip focus application


## Technical constraints
- Use SceneObject.isFocused to decide whether to blur


## Dependencies
- INT-1
- REQ-1


## Definition of done
- Null focus clears all highlighted objects


## Clarifying questions
- None
